National Board #: Manufacturer Name: Year Built:
Is the Manufacturer's Data Plate secured and legible?
Is the data plate free of corrosion?
Is the pressure rating proper for the product?
Are containers free of excessive corrosion damage, dents, gouges or other damage?
Are all container markings and decals in accordance with NFPA 58?
Are containers/saddles free of corrosion at masonry contact areas?
Are saddle pads in good condition?
Are all container openings (except relief valve connections) equipped with proper fixed restriction, back check, or internal valves and shutoff valves?
Are connections on containers greater than 2,000 gallon water capacity marked "vapor" or "liquid"?
Are all fittings that are subject to container pressure rated for at least 250 psig working pressure?
Are all unused openings plugged or capped?
Are pressure gauges in good condition and suitable for 250 psig service (such as 0 - 400 psig)?
Are liquid level gauges arranged and installed so that the liquid level can be accurately determined?
Is the relief valve marked for use with LP- Gas and labeled by an independent testing agency?
Is the relief capacity sufficient, as determined by NFPA 58?
Do relief valves communicate with the container vapor space and discharge upward, unobstructed to the open air?
Are relief valves on containers >2000 gallons water capacity equipped with vent stacks of proper diameter and length?
Are relief valve vent stacks on containers >2000 gallons water capacity equipped with breakaway couplings?
Do relief valves or vent stacks have loose- fitting protective caps or closures to prevent entry of foreign matter?
Are weep holes for moisture drainage open and is gas impingement of the container prevented?
Are the valve body seams leak-free?
Is the pneumatic control system in good working condition?
Are hydraulic operators in good working condition?
Is the thermal link intact and free of paint?
Are ESVs in good working condition and leak free?
Has an annual test been performed and documented as required by NFPA 58?
Is the pneumatic control system in good working condition?
Are remote emergency shutoff devices between 25 and 100 feet from the ESV and within the path of egress?
Is the thermal link intact and free of paint?
Are valves located so that they can be easily reached during normal operations and in an emergency?
Are valves in good condition and leak-free?
Do valves have the proper service pressure rating, equal to or greater than the maximum allowable working pressure of the container?
Are stairways well anchored and supported?
Are catwalk railings provided and in good condition?
Does decking design offer drainage and prevent accumulation?
Is the area within 10 feet of the containers free of weeds, long grass, rags, paper, wood or other loose or piled combustible debris?
Is protection against vehicular damage provided for the fitting housing, housing cover, tank connections and piping?
Is the container protected against corrosion by at least one of the following means:
a.) An external coating on the tank?
Are pipes free of corrosion damage, dents, gouges or other damage?
Are pipes adequately protected against physical damage by vehicles?
Are pipes properly marked "vapor" or "liquid" or color coded accordingly?
Are all flanges and fittings properly sized for the pressure rating, equal to or greater than the maximum allowable working pressure of the system?
Are all stainless steel flex connectors in good working condition (i.e., reinforcement braid is not damaged)?
Are all flow indicators and sight checks in proper working condition and leak-free?
Are all fittings and pipes leak-free?
Are hydrostatic relief valves installed in each section of piping in which liquid can be isolated between shut-off valves?
Are hydrostatic relief valves approved for use with LP-Gas?
Do the hydrostatic relief valves have pressure settings between 400 - 500 psig?
Are valves located so that they can be easily reached during normal operations and in an emergency?
Are valves in good condition and leak-free?
Do valves have the proper pressure rating, equal to or greater than the maximum allowable working pressure of the system?
Is metallic underground piping protected against corrosion by at least one of the following means:
a.) An external coating on piping?
Are pumps free of corrosion or other damage?
Are pump pads and/or foundations in good condition and properly supporting the pumps?
Are base plate bolts in place and properly securing the pump to that foundation?
Are strainers in good working condition (i.e., strainer screens free of debris) and leak-free?
Are hydrostatic relief valves installed in the appropriate location and in good working condition?
Are all stainless steel flex connectors in good working condition (i.e., reinforcement braid is not damaged)?
Are fittings and piping associated with the pump leak-free?
Are drive belts properly aligned and in good working condition?
For shaft coupling-driven pumps, are shaft couplings properly aligned?
For shaft coupling-driven pumps, are spacing bushings in good working condition?
For gear reduction-driven pumps, are universal joints and couplings properly aligned and in good working condition?
Are drive belt guards in place and secure?
Are pressure gauges in good condition (i.e., 0 - 400 psig)?
Are bypasses in good working condition and leak-free?
Are bypasses set at the appropriate pressure differential?
Are valves located so that they can be easily reached during normal operations and in an emergency?
Are valves in good condition and leak-free?
Do valves have the proper pressure rating, equal to or greater than the maximum allowable working pressure of the system?
Are bulkheads properly protected against vehicular damage?
Are bulkheads (i.e., structure and foundation) in good condition and properly supporting the bulkhead, especially in the event of an attempted pull-away?
Are pipe nipples and couplings that are attached to the bulkhead in good working condition and free of excessive wear?
Are all flanges and fittings properly sized for the pressure rating, equal to or greater than the maximum allowable working pressure of the system
Are all stainless steel flex connectors in good working condition (i.e., reinforcement braid is not damaged)?
Are all flow indicators and sight checks in proper working condition and leak-free?
Are hydrostatic relief valves installed in the appropriate location and in good working condition?
Are all fittings and pipes leak-free?
Are ESVs in good working condition and leak-free?
Has an annual test been performed and documented as required by NFPA 58
Is the pneumatic control system in good working condition?
Are remote emergency shutoff devices between 25 and 100 feet from the ESV and within the path of egress?
Are the hose covers free of exposed reinforcement?
Is wire braid reinforcement free of kinks and not flattened?
Are hoses free of soft spots when not under pressure, show no bulging under pressure, and have no loose outer coverings?
Are hose coupling assemblies secure and in good working condition?
Are the ACME threads, O-rings, or gaskets in good working condition (i.e., showing little sign of excessive wear)?
Are valves located so that they may be easily reached during normal operations and in an emergency?
Are valves in good condition and leak-free?
Do the valves have the proper pressure rating, equal to or greater than the maximum allowable working pressure of the system?
Are compressors free of corrosion or other damage?
Are compressor pads and/or foundations in good condition and properly supporting the compressors?
Are base plate bolts in place and securing the compressor to that foundation?
Is the crankcase oil properly filled?
Is the crankcase oil pressure properly set?
Has the oil filter been changed at the manufacturer's recommended interval?
Are strainers elements in good working condition (i.e., strainer screens free of debris) and leak-free?
Are pressure relief valves installed in the appropriate location and in good working condition?
Are all stainless steel flex connectors in good working condition (i.e., reinforcement braid is not damaged)?
Are all back check valves in proper working condition and leak-free?
Are fittings and piping associated with the compressor leak-free?
Are drive belts properly aligned, tension properly set, and in good working condition?
For direct drive compressors, are shaft couplings properly aligned and in good working condition?
Are drive belt guards in place and secure?
Are pressure gauges (suction and discharge) in good condition (i.e., 0 - 400 psig)?
Are valves located so that they can be easily reached during normal operations and in an emergency?
Are valves in good condition and leak-free?
Do valves have the proper pressure rating, equal to or greater than the required working pressure of the system?
Are all flanges and fittings properly sized for the pressure rating equal to or greater than the maximum allowable working pressure of the system?
Are all stainless steel flex connectors in good working condition (i.e., reinforcement braid is not damaged)?
Are all flow indicators and sight checks in proper working condition and leak free?
Are hydrostatic relief valves installed in the appropriate location and in good working condition?
Are all fittings and pipes leak-free?
Are ESVs in good working condition and leak-free?
Are ESVs and/or back checks (including thermal release) on riser ends of the liquid hoses in good working condition?
Are ESVS on riser ends of the vapor hose (including thermal release) in good working condition?
Has an annual test been performed and documented as required by NFPA 58?
Is the pneumatic control system in good working condition and free of leaks?
Are remote emergency shutoff devices between 25 and 100 feet from the ESV and within the path of egress?
Are the hose covers in good condition to prevent exposure of the reinforcement?
Is wire braid reinforcement free of kinks and not flattened?
Are hoses free of soft spots when not under pressure, show no bulging under pressure, and have no loose outer coverings?
Are hose coupling assemblies secure and in good working condition?
Are the ACME threads, O-rings, or gaskets in good working condition (i.e., showing little sign of excessive wear)?
Are loading arms leak-free and in good working condition?
Are the loading arm swing-joints properly lubricated?
Are all factory installed protective guards in place and secure?
Are valves located so that they can be easily reached during normal operations and in an emergency?
Are valves in good condition and leak-free?
Do valves have the proper pressure rating, equal to or greater than the required working pressure of the system?
Has the scale(s) been checked periodically using a certified/standard dead weight?
Is the scale(s) properly calibrated and been certified by the proper authority having jurisdiction?
Have all loops, pivots, and bearings been periodically lubricated?
Are the scale pit(s) and/or platform(s) free of any debris?
Are all actuators and control valves leak- free and in good working condition (i.e., proper fluid levels and proper alignment with scale)?
Are all sensing lines leak-free and in good working condition (i.e., free of kinks and proper alignment with the scale)?
Are the hose covers free of exposed reinforcement?
Is wire braid reinforcement free of kinks and not flattened?
Are hoses free of soft spots when not under pressure, show no bulging under pressure, and have no loose outer coverings?
Are hose coupling assemblies secure and in good working condition?
Are the ACME threads, O-rings, or gaskets in good working condition (i.e., showing little sign of excessive wear)?
Is the meter(s) properly calibrated or "proved" at the appropriate time intervals?
Is the seal(s) in place by the appropriate authority having jurisdiction?
Is the meter in good working condition and free of leaks?
Has the strainer been properly cleaned out of any debris?
Are the hose covers free of exposed reinforcement?
Is wire braid reinforcement free of kinks and not flattened?
Are hoses free of soft spots when not under pressure, show no bulging under pressure, and have no loose outer coverings?
Are hose coupling assemblies secure and in good working condition?
Are the ACME threads, O-rings, or gaskets in good working condition (i.e., showing little sign of excessive wear)?
Are pull-away couplings in place and in good working condition?
Is the vaporizer(s) leak-free and in good working condition?
Have pilot lights been cleaned on a regular basis?
On a periodic basis, have all strainers been cleaned at the inlet side of the vaporizer(s)?
Have heavy ends been cleaned from the vaporizer(s) and/or separator tank?
Have the burner openings, thermostat, and flue been cleaned?
Is the vaporizer(s) located in accordance with NFPA 58?
Is the first-stage or high-pressure regulator directly attached by flexible connectors to the vaporizer outlet or to the interconnected piping of manifolded vaporizers?
Are all first-stage and high-pressure regulators installed outside of buildings?

Are all regulators that are outside of buildings installed and protected so that their operation will not be affected by environmental elements (e.g., freezing rain, sleet, snow, ice, mud or debris) or insects?
Is the point of discharge on the regulator's relief device at least 3 feet horizontally away from any building opening that is below the level of the discharge?
Is the point of discharge on the regulator's relief device located at least 5 feet in any direction from any source of ignition or mechanical ventilation air intakes?
Are all electrical components and wiring in compliance with Table 6.20.2.2 (Electrical Area Classification) in NFPA 58-2004?
Are electrical control switches and wiring in compliance with Class 1, Group D, Division 1 or 2 (where applicable) in compliance with Table 6.20.2.2 (Electrical Area Classification) in NFPA 58-2004?
Are pump and/or compressor switches readily accessible to the operator?
Are electrical controls for equipment clearly marked or color-coded to indicate the on and off (stop) positions?
Is the electrical emergency shutdown located more than 20 ft (but less than 100 ft) from any dispensing devices, and prominently labeled?
Is electrical wiring, in Division 1 or 2 areas, installed in rigid conduit? Class 1, Group D in flexible sections?
For electric motors, are flexible connectors Class 1, Group D, Division 1 or 2 where applicable?
Are all seal-off fixtures filled with suitable putty and installed in the appropriate locations?
